subject: Mathematics
title: Calculus: Integration Quiz
description: Tests understanding of indefinite/definite integrals and the area-under-a-curve interpretation, from the Integration lesson of Introduction to Calculus.

questions.prompt: The indefinite integral ∫ xⁿ dx (for n ≠ -1) reverses which differentiation rule?
Why does every indefinite integral include a "+ C"?
options: Because integration always overestimates the true area
Because differentiating any constant gives zero, so many functions share the same derivative
Because C stands for the coordinates of the curve's midpoint
It is only a notational convention with no mathematical meaning

questions.prompt: What does a definite integral ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx compute?
options: The slope of the tangent line at x = a
The instantaneous rate of change at x = b
The exact area between the curve and the x-axis, from x = a to x = b
The value of f(x) at the midpoint of a and b

questions.rubricGuidance: Apply the power rule to each term: 6x² → 2x³, -4x → -2x², 1 → x. Correct answer: 2x³ - 2x² + x + C. Full credit requires all three terms correctly integrated and the constant of integration included.

expectedPoints.text: Integrates 6x² to 2x³ using the power rule
Includes the constant of integration C

questions.prompt: Calculate the definite integral of f(x) = x² from x = 0 to x = 2, and state what this value physically represents.
questions.rubricGuidance: Antiderivative is x³/3. Evaluate F(2) - F(0) = 8/3 - 0 = 8/3. This value represents the exact area between the curve f(x) = x² and the x-axis, between x = 0 and x = 2.

expectedPoints.text: States it represents the area under the curve between x=0 and x=2

questions.prompt: Explain how integration and differentiation relate to each other, and why integration is described as the reverse of differentiation.

keyPoints.text: Differentiation finds a rate of change, geometrically the slope of the tangent line
Integration finds a total accumulated quantity, most commonly the area under a curve
Indefinite integration reverses the power rule used in differentiation
The +C constant exists because differentiating any constant produces zero
A definite integral is evaluated by finding the antiderivative F(x) and computing F(b) minus F(a)
Because differentiation and integration undo each other, they are treated as inverse operations
A definite integral gives the exact area between a curve and the x-axis over an interval
